Two halves: what a provider still owes us and the sweep is chasing, and what has landed as a file. Both are counted per channel below, and the inventory holds the breakdown.", "col": 12}, "id": "a1"}, {"type": "header", "data": {"text": "Owed to us", "col": 12}, "id": "a2"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "One retry policy, spent by two ledgers: five attempts over about thirty-one hours, after which the row is Abandoned and inert. To Re-fetch is a fetch that failed and still carries the address to try again \u2014 whether anything is trying depends on the retry switch, which these figures do not read. Not Yet Published is a recording the provider has not published at all, and Without a Source is its WhatsApp twin \u2014 the inbound event named media and carried no address. Neither is re-fetchable, whatever the sweep does. The two are counted apart because one is ours to fix and the other is not. Abandoned is the terminal set, not a window: the recording ledger drops its own terminal rows at ninety days, the WhatsApp one keeps them.", "col": 12}, "id": "a3"}, {"type": "number_card", "data": {"number_card_name": "Recordings To Re-fetch", "col": 4}, "id": "a4"}, {"type": "number_card", "data": {"number_card_name": "Recordings Not Yet Published", "col": 4}, "id": "a5"}, {"type": "number_card", "data": {"number_card_name": "Recordings Abandoned", "col": 4}, "id": "a6"}, {"type": "number_card", "data": {"number_card_name": "WhatsApp Media To Re-fetch", "col": 4}, "id": "a7"}, {"type": "number_card", "data": {"number_card_name": "WhatsApp Media Without a Source", "col": 4}, "id": "a8"}, {"type": "number_card", "data": {"number_card_name": "WhatsApp Media Abandoned", "col": 4}, "id": "a9"}, {"type": "header", "data": {"text": "Landed", "col": 12}, "id": "a10"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A file's bytes belong in Azure. Anything still on the application server is counted here, and while the offload automation is armed the figure is expected to be zero \u2014 above zero means bytes are sitting on a disk that no backup and no retention policy covers. With offload switched off every file is legitimately local and the figure is not a fault. Site Storage is every File row on this site, this app's and every other app's, which is what the inventory's Other rows account for. The three switches these figures depend on \u2014 Azure offload, recording retry and WhatsApp media retry \u2014 are armed under Engine Switches.", "col": 12}, "id": "a11"}, {"type": "number_card", "data": {"number_card_name": "Files on VM Disk", "col": 4}, "id": "a12"}, {"type": "number_card", "data": {"number_card_name": "Site Storage", "col": 4}, "id": "a13"}, {"type": "header", "data": {"text": "Inventory", "col": 12}, "id": "a14"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Asset Inventory is the whole picture on one screen: in flight, retrying, abandoned, files, bytes still on the server and space consumed, a row per channel with a total. It replaces asking the database directly.", "col": 12}, "id": "a15"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Asset Inventory", "col": 4}, "id": "a16"}, {"type": "spacer", "data": {"col": 12}, "id": "a17"}, {"type": "header", "data": {"text": "Read the rows", "col": 12}, "id": "a18"}, {"type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each figure above is a count over one of these tables. Call Media carries a recording's state, its attempt count and the error the last attempt returned; WhatsApp Messages carries the same for media a message is owed; Files is every artifact that landed.", "col": 12}, "id": "a19"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Call Media", "col": 4}, "id": "a20"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "WhatsApp Messages", "col": 4}, "id": "a21"}, {"type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Files", "col": 4}, "id": "a22"}, {"type": "spacer", "data": {"col": 12}, "id": "a23"}]
